resolved_levels_check: PASS - Mega Machamp 48-1-2=45, Gholdengo 48+0-2=46, Dhelmise 48+0-2=46, Decidueye 48+1-2=47, all matching the driver at level_cap 48. No --cap adjustment.

attempts.note: Gengar + Incineroar + Spiritomb + Togekiss + Alakazam + Weavile. Duncan opened with the best two-card sequence in this block - Machamp's priority Bullet Punch broke Gengar's Focus Sash and Gholdengo's Shadow Ball then killed it through the hole, on the same turn. Mega Machamp's No Guard Drain Punch then one-shot a 194 HP Incineroar. Spiritomb's Fighting immunity plus a Will-O-Wisp was what turned it: a burned Mega Machamp could not break either of my last two bodies, and Togekiss's Flying and Fairy damage cleaned up the three Ghosts.

strategy_checks.check: Machamp and Choice Scarf Gholdengo apply coordinated physical and special pressure
strategy_checks.result: PASS - and better than the dossier claims
strategy_checks.evidence: turn 1, Machamp's Bullet Punch (priority, chosen specifically to break a Focus Sash) landed first and Gholdengo's 2x Shadow Ball then KO'd Gengar through the broken Sash. That is a real two-card combination, not two solos, and it cost me my best answer to the room on turn one.

strategy_checks.check: Gholdengo chooses a useful locked attack rather than assuming Make It Rain can be repeated
strategy_checks.evidence: it locked into Shadow Ball, the 2x option on the board, rather than Make It Rain and its Special Attack drop.

strategy_checks.evidence: I withheld Gengar's Taunt and Spiritomb's Will-O-Wisp from Gholdengo for the whole battle because both would simply fail. The ability shaped my play without ever needing to trigger.

strategy_checks.evidence: Gholdengo had a guaranteed 2x KO available on turn 1 and correctly took it instead of Tricking. It died that same turn.

strategy_checks.check: Mega Machamp's No Guard means perfect accuracy on everything it throws
strategy_checks.evidence: every Machamp attack in the battle connected, and Drain Punch one-shot a full-HP 194 HP Incineroar while healing itself.

strategy_checks.check: Dhelmise's Anchor Shot traps the switch-out
strategy_checks.evidence: Dhelmise selected Anchor Shot on turn 4 but was flinched by a Serene Grace Air Slash before it resolved, and died that turn. Decidueye's Spirit Shackle did land twice, so the trapping half of the wreck's identity was at least represented.

protect_note: Duncan's side used no Protect at all. Dhelmise and Decidueye both carry it and on every board they had a better action. No empty guarding to report.

ai_defects.board: Machamp (holding Machampite, Mega unused) + Gholdengo vs Gengar + Incineroar
ai_defects.chosen: Machamp used Bullet Punch without Mega Evolving, and only Mega Evolved on turn 2
ai_defects.problem: Mega Evolution is free - it costs no action and applies before the turn resolves - so holding it back for a turn simply gives up a turn of the Mega's stats for nothing. Machamp spent turn 1 in its base form and Mega Evolved on turn 2 instead.
ai_defects.better: Mega Evolve on turn 1 alongside the same Bullet Punch. There is no board on which delaying a Mega Evolution by a turn is correct here, since the stone carries no downside and the form change does not reveal information the opponent could not already see from the held item.
ai_defects.note: Worth checking against the other Mega owners in this block: Foster's Slowbro, Darrin's Gyarados, Carolina's Gardevoir and Norman's Staraptor all Mega Evolved on their entry turn, so this looks specific to a Mega that starts the battle on the field rather than a general rule.

calibration_reasoning: Won on the first attempt with two player faints. AGENTS.md sets a level-increase review at a first-attempt win with fewer than three faints, so I reviewed it and am recording the justified exception: the brief's own threshold is 'won with 2+ faints or after a real fight - keep', and this was plainly a real fight. Duncan is a regular-class trainer with four members and he removed Gengar and Incineroar - two of my six best answers - inside two turns, one of them through a correctly executed Sash-break combination and one to a No Guard Drain Punch that one-shot a 194 HP body. A regular that costs a fully optimized cap-48 party two premium bodies does not need a level. No change.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep, and the dossier's closing judgement deserves a correction. It says 'the honest gap is that four strong solos never combine; this is a very good pile rather than a team.' That is not what happened. Machamp's Bullet Punch into Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is a deliberate, executable Focus Sash break, and the AI found it on turn one unprompted - two cards, one kill, on the exact body that was built to answer the room. The wreck also has a coherent second idea in its two trapping moves, Anchor Shot and Spirit Shackle, which punish exactly the switching a player wants to do against a Choice Scarf Trick user. If anything is worth changing it is smaller than the dossier suggests: Gholdengo's Trick is the one card that never has a good moment, because a Scarf user with a 2x attack available should always attack, and by the time Trick is the right play Gholdengo is usually dead. Swapping it for a fourth attack, or accepting it as a rarely-fired option, is the honest call. No species, ability, item or EV change recommended.
legality_problems_found: None. Gholdengo's zero Attack IVs are correctly set for a special attacker, as the dossier states.
